Calculate batting statistics from reviewed plays

Source: R/calculate_batting_stats.R
calculate_batting_stats.Rd

Calculate counting and rate statistics for each game, team, and player. Input can come from import_scorecards() or another source that follows the same column contract. Rows represent distinct scorecard entries; identical-looking rows are not automatically deduplicated.

Usage

calculate_batting_stats(scorecards)

Arguments

scorecards

A data frame with the seven columns returned by import_scorecards(). All entries must have needs_review = FALSE and known confidence. Review uncertain entries before calculation.

Value

One row per game_id, team, and player, in first-appearance order. Counting columns are PA, AB, H, BB (including intentional walks), HBP, SF, SH, CI, and TB. Rate columns are BA, OBP, SLG, and OPS, without rounding. Zero denominators produce NA_real_. No rows are returned for players with only blank/automatic-runner markers.

Details

BA = H/AB; OBP = (H+BB+HBP)/(AB+BB+HBP+SF); SLG = TB/AB; OPS = OBP+SLG. Sacrifice bunts and catcher interference count as plate appearances but are excluded from AB and the OBP denominator. Sacrifice flies are excluded from AB but included in the OBP denominator. Errors and fielder's choices count as at-bats, not hits. Double plays contribute one batter at-bat. Automatic runners are not plate appearances.

Only the explicitly supported play labels are accepted. An unrecognized event must be reviewed rather than silently dropped. This first version does not estimate missing plays or resolve duplicate player names.

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "demo_plays.csv", package = "daimondstats")
plays <- import_scorecards(path, "demo-01")
calculate_batting_stats(plays)
#>   game_id      team    player PA AB H BB HBP SF SH CI TB   BA       OBP  SLG
#> 1 demo-01 Demo Owls Alex Demo  6  4 3  1   0  1  0  0  7 0.75 0.6666667 1.75
#> 2 demo-01 Demo Owls  Sam Demo  4  0 0  1   1  0  1  1  0   NA 1.0000000   NA
#>        OPS
#> 1 2.416667
#> 2       NA
